hero.title: Flyer builder pattern
hero.description: Use FlyerBuilderSection to let a visitor make a printable flyer or an image from a photo, a few details and a phone number, all in the browser.

example.title: Example
example.description: The lost-dog flyer running live. Add a photo and a phone number to see the preview, then print it or download it. The flyer follows the site's language.

standard.title: Usage rules
items: Use `FlyerBuilderSection` when a visitor should make their own flyer (lost dog, found dog) from a photo, a few details and a phone number. For ready-made flyers the rescue publishes, use `FlyerLibrarySection`.

A flyer type is a `FlyerSpec` (data): fixed wording per language, palette, layout and fields. Start from `lostDogFlyerSpec` or `foundDogFlyerSpec` in `FlyerBuilderSection.specs.ts` and spread it to change wording. Import the `FlyerSpec` type from the pattern; never re-declare it.
The flyer carries no organization name, logo or phone number. The phone number is the visitor's own.
Everything runs in the browser. Nothing is uploaded, the photo's location data is dropped, and the pattern makes no network calls, so it needs no CSP registry entry.
The photo is never cropped: it is drawn whole, at its own proportions, inside the page margins.

Every visible string comes from the site through `labels` (`FlyerBuilderLabels`). Organization-specific lines, such as a guide's advice about names or rewards, live in the site's locale file, never in the pattern.
`headlineFontUrl` is the site's own same-origin woff2 for the heavy headline face. Leave it off to use the Impact / Arial Narrow fallback. Never point it at a CDN.
`noScript` shows blank printable PDFs (one per language) when JavaScript is off. The route stays prerendered.
Print and download names come from `FlyerSpec.fileNamePrefix` (default `<id>-flyer`).
The page around the tool (header, breadcrumb, language toggle, help links) belongs to the site. A new route starts `noindex` and in the sitemap exclusions until the client approves listing it.
Phone numbers are US (NANP) only. Street-address and reward text is flagged with an advisory note, never blocked.
